cutoff_window.policy: Only public web sources with visible publication or update dates inside the last two days relative to run time qualify. Missing, ambiguous, future-dated, boundary-only, stale, or upstream-only entity updates are excluded or recorded as routing notes.

federation_boundary.rule: This collector keeps local AI-assisted-development practice, workflow, governance, verification, adoption, and implementation implications. Broad companies, products, models, developer tools, agentic frameworks, MCP servers, and general techniques remain upstream-owned.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Updates to Copilot Code Reviews for Azure Repos
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Azure DevOps described recent Copilot Code Review changes for Azure Repos, including Lite/Balanced effort levels at project and repository scope, batch resolution of review comments after applying suggestions, and new audit-log events for enablement, agent-pool, custom-instruction, effort-level, and automatic-review branch-policy changes.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The update turns AI code review configuration into governed project metadata rather than hidden tool state. Local practice coverage should track audit-log evidence, default effort-level policy, and comment-resolution workflow as control points for teams using AI review in regulated or multi-repository settings.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Broad product coverage belongs to the upstream AI wiki; this artifact keeps only the local review-governance implication.
Broad developer-platform coverage is upstream-owned; the local finding is about AI review configuration evidence.

follow_up_notes: During ingest, consider whether audit-log events belong under governance-and-risk or verification-and-evals as review evidence.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Evo ADS Govern Agent Behavior Goes GA: Bringing MCP Usage Under Control
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Snyk announced general availability of Govern Agent Behavior in Evo Agentic Development Security, starting with MCP Governance. The capability discovers MCP servers, defines allowed servers, observes out-of-policy use, and can log or block MCP usage at runtime across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and GitHub Copilot through endpoint hooks.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The source frames MCP governance as runtime enforcement at the moment an agent calls a tool, not only CI scanning or after-the-fact inventory. Local practice pages can use this as current evidence for MCP allowlists, endpoint enforcement, audit evidence, and package-install/tool-supply-chain risk boundaries.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GitLab and Claude Code: Fast, compliant AI
qualifying_findings.date_basis: Article page and archive show Published on: September 29, 2026.
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitLab described using Duo Agent Platform as the governed execution plane around Claude Code for government agencies. The article emphasizes scoped, logged, reviewable actions, shared project context, merge request gates, audit trails tied to merge requests, model-provider flexibility, and self-hosted deployment options for data residency and network restrictions.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The update is useful local evidence for the operating-model claim that coding-agent output needs a governed system of record, merge-request gates, and audit trails independent of which model or coding interface produced the code.

qualifying_findings.source_title: HydraFusion in VS Code and the GitHub Copilot app
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub expanded the HydraFusion research preview to VS Code and the GitHub Copilot app. The changelog says HydraFusion orchestrates multiple models through single, cascade, and critique workflows, including a read-only critic from a different model family, and adds clearer transparency, more frequent real-time progress updates, and status for long tasks.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local implication is not the model-routing product itself, but the practice pattern: agent workflow selection, independent critic roles, quality gates, and progress/status reporting are becoming explicit user-facing controls for long-running coding tasks.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Broad product/research-preview coverage belongs upstream; this finding retains local workflow-selection and progress-reporting implications.

follow_up_notes: Could inform local application-pattern notes on critic workflows and status/progress design.
Do not duplicate the HydraFusion entity page locally.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GitHub Copilot code review, tuned to how your team works
qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub described Copilot code review as using repository AGENTS.md files, custom instructions without the earlier 4,000-character cap, MCP servers, custom agent skills, issue and pull request history, content exclusions, and Lite/Balanced review depth to produce cited review comments grounded in team standards and project context.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is direct practice-level material for durable instructions, retrieval into review, MCP/custom-skill context, content-exclusion boundaries, and AI-review depth controls. It supports a downstream lens on how teams externalize standards so AI reviewers do not operate only on diffs.

upstream_owned_entities.reason: Product background belongs upstream; local coverage should focus on durable instructions, context retrieval, and review governance.
Broad MCP server catalog/background belongs upstream; local coverage should focus on governed retrieval into reviews.

follow_up_notes: Strong candidate for ingest into prompt-and-instructions and verification-and-evals leaves.
Verify any custom-instruction limit claim against product documentation before turning it into a durable rule.
